question: What was the main focus of India’s Second Five Year Plan with respect to the economy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Heavy industrialisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Five Year Plan of India (1956-1961) was based on the Nehru-Mahalanobis model, which emphasized the growth of heavy industries and industrialization.
 
• Its primary goal was to establish a strong industrial base to accelerate economic development and achieve self-reliance in production.
 
• The plan focused on the development of core industries such as steel, heavy machinery, chemicals, and engineering goods.
 
• It aimed to reduce dependency on foreign imports by promoting indigenous production in heavy industries.
 
• The plan also emphasized the role of the public sector in industrial development, with major investments in infrastructure and factories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Expansion of services:**

 
 
• While the service sector contributes significantly to India's economy today, it was not the focus during the Second Five Year Plan.
 
• Services like healthcare, education, and transportation were emphasized in later plans to complement industrial and agricultural growth.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of tourism:**
 
 
• Tourism was not a priority under the Second Five Year Plan as it focused on industrialization and economic self-reliance.
 
• Tourism development emerged as a focus area in later decades as the government recognized its potential for generating revenue and employment.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution was introduced in India during the mid-1960s, after the Second Five Year Plan, to address food security and agricultural productivity.
 
• The revolution primarily focused on high-yielding crops, irrigation, and the use of fertilizers and pesticides.
